objections.text: The reasoning says PostgreSQL drops the final edge and returns 27 rows. The input contains 27 edges, so dropping the final edge leaves 26 result rows. The case remains a date-rounding/MAXRECURSION attack, but its stated non-error outcome does not match the values sent.

The two rows for assembly 2, component 1 have the same StartDate. They violate the source table's unique key on ProductAssemblyID, ComponentID and StartDate, so this input is outside the source schema preconditions.

The BillOfMaterials quantities 0.05 through 0.45 violate the source check requiring PerAssemblyQty >= 1.00, and product 5 has a negative StandardCost contrary to the source Product check. The diamond input is not valid source data.

Products 2 and 3 both use Name 'P2'. Production.Product has a case-insensitive unique key on Name, so the repeated value used to satisfy the top-ties claim cannot occur under the source schema preconditions.

Product names 'Bolt', 'BOLT' and 'bolt ' collide under the source case-insensitive, trailing-space-insensitive unique key on Production.Product.Name. The input cannot be loaded into the source table with its constraints.

The three identical BillOfMaterials rows violate the source unique key; the negative PerAssemblyQty violates its >= 1.00 check; and the negative Product.ListPrice violates the source Product check. This overflow case is outside the source schema preconditions.

The 2 -> 3 row ends on 2019-12-31 but starts on 2020-01-01. That violates the source BillOfMaterials check requiring EndDate after StartDate (or NULL), so the filtered-cycle input is not valid source data.
